title_ar: الشيخ الددو يلقي كلمة في افتتاح المؤتمر السادس لمنتدى كوالالمبور للفكر والحضارة
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Delivers an Address at the Opening of the Sixth Conference of the Kuala Lumpur Forum for Thought and Civilisation
body_ar: افتتحت صباح اليوم 11 -12 – 2022م -بالعاصمة التركية استنطبول - أشغال المؤتمر السادس لمنتدى كوالالمبور للفكر والحضارة، تحت شعار " الاستئناف الحضاري ومشاريع الإحياء في الأمة الإسلامية (الجذور – الواقع – المستقبل)" وذلك بمشاركة فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو نائب رئيس المنتدى وفضيلة الدكتور عبد الرزاق مقري الأمين العام للمنتدى وجمع غفير من علماء الأمة ومفكريها وقادة نهضتها. وقد افتُـتح المؤتمر بتلاوة عطرة من الذكر الحكيم تلاها عرض فيديو تعريفي بالمنتدى، ثم كلمة الأمين العام وكلمة نائب الرئيس، وعرض فيديو عن منجزات المنتدى. الأمين العام للمنتدى فضيلة د. عبد الرزاق مقري ألقى كلمة رحب فيها بالحضور متحدثا عن أبرز العقبات التي تواجه الأمة في الوقت الراهن وكيفية تجاوزها. من جانبه تحدث فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو نائب رئيس المنتدى عما واجهته الأمة من تحديات، وما يجب على أبناء الأمة فعله في سبيل نهضتها ورقيها ودفع الظلم عنها ثم تحدث فضيلته عن سقوط الخلافة وتشتت الأمة واحتلال بلدانها وتغلب القوى الغربية عليها. كما دعا إلى اشتغال المصلحين بالتربية والعلم وإصلاح ذات البين وإقالة العثرات ونبذ الخلاف. كما تخلل حفل الافتتاح تقديم عدد من الدروع وشهادات التقدير للشخصيات والجهات المشاركة في نهضة الأمة والدفاع عن قضاياها. هذا ويستمر المؤتمر لثلاثة أيام يناقش المشاركون فيه مشاريع إحياء الامة، ليقدموا مجموعة من التوصيات والمقترحات التي من شأنها أن ترفع بالأمة وتساهم في نهضتها.
body_en: This morning, 11-12-2022, in the Turkish capital Istanbul, the proceedings of the sixth conference of the Kuala Lumpur Forum for Thought and Civilisation opened under the banner "Civilisational Resumption and the Projects of Revival in the Islamic Ummah (Roots — Present Reality — Future)", with the participation of His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, deputy president of the Forum, His Eminence Dr Abderrazak Makri, secretary-general of the Forum, and a great throng of the Ummah's scholars, its thinkers and the leaders of its renaissance. The conference was opened with a fragrant recitation from the Wise Remembrance, followed by a video presenting the Forum, then the address of the secretary-general and the address of the deputy president, and a video about the Forum's achievements. The Forum's secretary-general, His Eminence Dr Abderrazak Makri, gave an address in which he welcomed those attending and spoke about the foremost obstacles facing the Ummah at the present time and how they are to be overcome. For his part, His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, deputy president of the Forum, spoke about the challenges the Ummah has faced, and about what the sons of the Ummah are obliged to do for the sake of its renaissance and its advancement and the repelling of injustice from it; His Eminence then spoke about the fall of the caliphate, the scattering of the Ummah, the occupation of its lands and the ascendancy of the Western powers over it. He also called upon those who work for reform to occupy themselves with upbringing and with knowledge, with reconciling people to one another, with helping others past their stumbles, and with casting off discord. The opening ceremony also included the presentation of a number of plaques and certificates of appreciation to the figures and bodies taking part in the Ummah's renaissance and the defence of its causes. The conference continues for three days, in which the participants discuss projects for the Ummah's revival, so as to put forward a set of recommendations and proposals such as would raise up the Ummah and contribute to its renaissance.

flags.note: al-istiʾnāf al-ḥaḍārī is a set phrase in modern Islamic thought for resuming a civilisational trajectory held to have been interrupted, and 'resumption' rather than 'renewal' is what the Arabic says. The Forum may have its own English name for the conference; if so that should override this rendering.

flags.note: yajib carries the glossary's wājib. The five-rulings mapping forbids rendering it by a bare 'must', so 'are obliged to' is used. Note that this is the news desk summarising a conference address, not the Sheikh issuing a ruling, and the site should not display it as one.

translator_notes: A news report by the site's news desk. The account of what the Sheikh said is the desk's summary, not his words.

The date inside the body is written 11 -12 – 2022 with an en dash, which in Mauritanian and Maghrebi usage is day-month-year: 11 December 2022. The CMS publishes the report on 20 December. Both have been preserved; the ISO date follows the CMS stamp, as elsewhere in the corpus.

استنطبول is the source's spelling of Istanbul and is a misspelling of the standard اسطنبول, which the same record uses correctly further down. Preserved in body_ar and not corrected, per style guide section 11.
The body contains a CMS artefact: افتُـتح carries a stray damma and a tatweel inside the word. Preserved in body_ar, silently normal in body_en, flagged here rather than fixed.
الذكر الحكيم is rendered 'the Wise Remembrance', a name for the Qur'an; it is not a separate scripture.
